beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Yash Saraf. This film pitches my final project, and nothing in it is built yet. I first asked whether AI can answer my GitHub Actions questions. The better question is whether it can show where its answers come from.

show.event: replaces it with: show where its answers come from

props.text: Can AI answer my Actions questions
props.replacementWords: show where its answers come from

beats.motion_claim: The writer types 'Can AI answer my Actions questions' and corrects it to 'Can AI show where its answers come from'.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Here's what I will build. Actions Docs Q and A will be a command-line tool that answers questions about GitHub Actions, using GitHub's own documentation.

shot.visual_intent: A stack of doc pages drops onto the stage; a question card slides in; an ink arc joins the question to the docs.
shot.motion_claim: A stack of doc pages drops onto the stage; a question card slides in; an ink arc joins the question to the docs.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It will search the docs for the passage that holds the answer. Then a small model, running free on my laptop, will write a short answer from that passage only, and quote it.

shot.visual_intent: A scan line sweeps the docs stack and the top page lifts with its passage dot; a dark model block appears and an answer slip rises out of it.
shot.motion_claim: A scan line sweeps the docs stack and the top page lifts with its passage dot; a dark model block appears and an answer slip rises out of it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Next, a script will check the quote, word for word, against the docs. If it matches, the answer ships with its source. If it doesn't, the tool shows the passage instead. No quote, no answer.

shot.visual_intent: A quote strip slides onto its line on the page and a check lands; a second, reworded strip fails to fit, bounces back, and gets a cross.
shot.motion_claim: A quote strip slides onto its line on the page and a check lands; a second, reworded strip fails to fit, bounces back, and gets a cross.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be a public GitHub repository: the tool, a script that fetches one pinned version of the docs, about fifty test questions, and a scored report.

shot.visual_intent: A long shelf labelled GitHub repo; the model block, a pinned docs stack, a row of test cards, and a report with grey bars drop onto it in turn.
shot.motion_claim: A long shelf labelled GitHub repo; the model block, a pinned docs stack, a row of test cards, and a report with grey bars drop onto it in turn.

beats.narration_text: Before pitching it, I tried what already exists, on October eleventh, with three questions from my own workflows. The docs site's keyword search listed the page holding the answer for just one of the three.

shot.visual_intent: Three question cards arrive; a docs-search window fills with result bars for each; crosses land beside two cards and a check beside one; '1 of 3' appears. Drawn from the 2026-10-11 screenshots.
shot.motion_claim: Three question cards arrive; a docs-search window fills with result bars for each; crosses land beside two cards and a check beside one; '1 of 3' appears. Drawn from the 2026-10-11 screenshots.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Ask Copilot, built into that search, and the Claude desktop app both matched the docs on all three. But Copilot listed its sources for only one, and Claude cited none.

shot.visual_intent: Two windows, Copilot and Claude; three answer slips land in each with checks; one source dot attaches to one Copilot slip, none to Claude's. Drawn from the 2026-10-11 screenshots.
shot.motion_claim: Two windows, Copilot and Claude; three answer slips land in each with checks; one source dot attaches to one Copilot slip, none to Claude's. Drawn from the 2026-10-11 screenshots.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: So mine is not meant to give better answers. What it adds is the exact sentence each answer came from, checked in the docs, instead of a link to a whole page.

shot.visual_intent: Two pages side by side: on the right one line is highlighted with a source dot and a check; on the left a frame draws around the whole page.
shot.motion_claim: Two pages side by side: on the right one line is highlighted with a source dot and a check; on the left a frame draws around the whole page.

beats.narration_text: It will also run free, on my own laptop. The docs search notes that GitHub keeps the questions asked there. My tool will send nothing anywhere.

shot.visual_intent: The docs and model block drop onto a laptop; a cloud draws on the right and question cards stack into it; a line from the laptop toward the cloud draws and is cut with a cross.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? I'm aiming for AI developer, DevOps, or cloud engineer roles, so the reader is a hiring manager or engineer on one of those teams. In the first minute, they read the results table, then open one test question and compare the expected passage with the tool's answer. No install needed.

shot.visual_intent: A README page with an empty results table; a sixty-second ring draws; one test card slides out with two slips side by side and a check between them.
shot.motion_claim: A README page with an empty results table; a sixty-second ring draws; one test card slides out with two slips side by side and a check between them.

beats.narration_text: What will it prove? That I can ground answers in a source, verify them with a script, hold a model to a fixed output shape, and evaluate it honestly, on about fifty questions, ten of which the docs don't cover.

shot.visual_intent: Four objects pop in a row on cue: a page with a source dot, a check, a slip with fixed slots, and a tray of test cards, two of them left empty.

beats.narration_text: What's out: agent loops, a web interface, other docs, and any claim that it beats Copilot or Claude. And it never answers from the model's memory.

beats.narration_text: The first piece is search alone, with no model: my three questions plus two more, checking whether the right passage lands in the top three. A dated results file in the repo will show it ran.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk is search missing. The docs' keyword search missed two of my three, and mine starts the same way. If plain-English questions keep missing, I'll add a free model that matches by meaning, and compare the two.

shot.visual_intent: A question card sends a solid keyword lane to the docs, which lifts the wrong page and gets a cross; a second, grey 'meaning' lane draws below, still planned.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. I already build C I pipelines: GitHub Actions runs in my three public repos from twenty twenty-five. Building search, running a local model, and measuring answers are new to me. It interests me, and that's why I want to explore it further.
